Where the project actually is
Before anything else: my memory of this project was stale by six slices. It said Slice 47 was in progress; the reconstructed tree is at Slice 52, landed and green. I've corrected course rather than authoring against a tree that doesn't exist. This is the second time this has happened (Slice 51's narrative records the first), and the reconstruction from dump.txt is again what caught it.

Reconstruction result: 363 file records parsed, 361 verified against their SHA-256 exactly. The two exceptions are both by design — export.sh contains the dump delimiter as literal text, and LICENSE is elided to metadata and hash.

Your last run was clean: total: 1233, failed: 0 against _CHANGES.md's prediction of 1233. §18's arithmetic has now matched to the digit for five consecutive slices.

What Slice 53 is
MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md Stage 4c — images on the guest's menu, which the plan itself calls "the half that was actually asked for." Everything before it built the schema (4a) and the administrator's form and route (4b); §11.1 still renders no picture, and IMenuItemImageDirectory.ListAsync is still a read with no caller.

Two design decisions I've settled while reading
1. Alt text survives a replace, and is set by its own verb. The plan says only "one ALTER with a DEFAULT ''" and "a field on the item's picture form." Putting it on the attach form alone creates a trap: the attach form requires a file, so fixing a typo in the caption would mean re-uploading the photograph — minting a new identifier, busting every browser cache, and writing a replaced event that replaced nothing. So alt_text is carried forward by AttachMenuItemImageAsync from the row it deletes, and changed in place by a new SetMenuItemImageAltTextAsync with its own alt_text_changed event type. AttachMenuItemImageAsync's signature doesn't change at all, and neither does the attach form.

2. A finding: the plan's own justification for alt_text is false as written (F-103). It says "an <img> with no alternative text on a menu is a card a screen reader renders as nothing." But the guest card is a <button> containing the name and price as text, so with alt="" its accessible name is already "Grilled salmon $24.00" — correct and sufficient. The sentence conflates a missing alt attribute (which does announce a filename) with alt="" (which is correctly skipped). The real rule is the one §11.4 already follows: always emit alt, from the stored value, "" when nobody wrote one — so the caption is announced only when it says something the name does not.

Verified as safe so far
The E2E harness locates span.order-menu-name, span.order-menu-price and span.order-menu-description as descendants of button.order-menu-choice, so wrapping them in a new .order-menu-body element to get the thumbnail beside them cannot break scenario 17.
ContentSecurityPolicyContractTests tests off-origin by looking for :// or a leading //; src="@MenuImageRoutes.ForImage(…)" passes, and the tree keeps at least one <img> so the non-vacuity guard holds.
0004's DO-block gave every menu_item_event CHECK a name, and 0005 widened the vocabulary by dropping it by name — that's the precedent 0007 follows for menu_item_image_event_type_vocabulary. The two existing payload biconditionals need no restating, since alt_text_changed carries neither a content type nor a byte length.
§16.4's counted-class floor (MinimumCountedClasses = 28) and the paragraphs for MenuItemImageTests (11 assertions) and MenuItemImageSurfaceContractTests (6 assertions) are the prose that will need moving.
